action_summary: The owner asked a fifth time why the most advanced coding actions cannot be given once and kept. Four documents written on 2026-11-12 (#6733, #6734, #6736, #6744) pointed at one obstacle -- FAIL_CLOSED__COMPUTER_EXECUTION_REQUIRES_ADMITTED_CONFINEMENT, 19 of 38 realistic advanced-coding sentences, with confinement_v1.py built as its release condition and 'wire the seam' priced as the next work item. None of them ran the counterfactual, which this tree's own law says is the only instrument that finds a cause rather than a symptom. This round runs it. First re-measured on this base: the wall had GROWN to 21 of 38 (the 19 was already stale when quoted a fourth time). Then canonical/tools/lift_the_refusal_and_see_what_remains_v1.py -- four stages in disposable git clone --no-local clones, host git status byte-identical throughout -- and the result refutes the chain: S1 lifting computer_execution_boundary_v1.refuses_execution buys 0 of 21 (21 of 21 still refuse). Instrumenting every emitter of the status string found the dominant source is NOT the boundary: it is live_brain_route_admission_v1._serve_by_acting, an automatic-computer-discovery refusal that stamps the boundary's status, firing for 18 of 21. Underneath, composer_route_v1.execute_chain and live_integrated_brain_v1 both RE-DERIVED the boundary's rule from its three small predicates instead of asking refuses_execution, which its docstring calls the single decision every execution site must use -- so with the boundary lifted, 3 of 21 still refused with the boundary's status, emitted by a copy no change to the boundary can reach. A release condition admitted once would have been silently ignored, and the wiring diff four documents recommended would have measured as ineffective and been reverted. FIXED additively: _chain_refuses and _plan_refuses now ask the decision (the repair row split repair=False then repair=True, exactly as its docstring specifies). Pinned by canonical/tests/test_one_decision_spelled_once_v1, 7/7: every one of 153 registry ids moves with a substituted decision, no runtime module re-derives the rule, every existing refusal is byte-identical, and the lift now propagates (S1 21->18, S2 3->0) while S0 stays 21. LAST, the thing nobody had tried: S3 binds the arguments each capability's own action_template declares, and python.source.symbols.index.ast and python.source.taint_flow.v1 execute end to end with output_verified True -- two full capabilities working at the point 21 of 21 refusals had said the obstacle was confinement. THE LIMITING FACTOR IS BINDING, NOT CONFINEMENT, and the label was the defect: three different refusals emitted one status string, so nine rounds measured the label.

2. De-duplicate the decision so a future release propagates -- chosen: additive, 7/7 pinned, refusals byte-identical
3. Bind declared arguments and measure the gain -- chosen: 2 of 21 execute end to end, the largest single move measured this round
4. Wire the confinement seam -- rejected by measurement: 0 of 21
5. Lift the automatic-discovery refusal -- rejected: not an agent's decision, and it is 18 of the 21
obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Wiring the seam was the top-ranked route in four documents and is refuted by its own counterfactual. Lifting discovery would release real authority this round has no mandate for. De-duplication and binding are additive, keep every refusal, and are measured.

obs_verification.synthetic_verification_necessity: The oracle is the door itself: the instrument asks the real front door in disposable clones, before and after the fix, and the fix's claim is a substitution experiment over all 153 registry ids plus byte-identical refusal shapes. It can fail in both directions -- S0 rising would mean the fix released something, S1 not falling would mean the de-duplication did not land. Both were measured; S0 stayed 21 and S1 fell 21 to 18.
